Review selective-turnover scope against route-specific terminology.
items.rationale: Use autophagy traitmech:000638 as the direct broader phenotype. This draft uses selective mitochondrial degradation, as named in the fission-yeast Results, without making membrane route universal. The 2007 yeast abstract reports selective and nonselective turnover with preferential microautophagy under its conditions. In contrast, issuing GO:0000423 names mitophagy specifically for selective macroautophagy and lists macromitophagy as exact; GO:0000424 micromitophagy is not its child. GO:0000422 autophagy of mitochondrion is broader and lists mitophagy as narrow. These nonobsolete biological-process records were directly resolved at https://www.ebi.ac.uk/QuickGO/services/ontology/go/terms/GO%3A0000422,GO%3A0000423,GO%3A0000424. Do not silently impose GO's route-specific usage on every microbial source, or assert an exact phenotype xref. Retain this interpretation for human review; omit exact synonyms including broad mitochondrial autophagy and route-specific macromitophagy. Protein/gene presence, puncta, organelle fragmentation, membrane depolarization, delivery without degradation, and nonspecific bulk capture alone are insufficient. The trait belongs to the microbial cell doing the turnover, not to a bacterium inducing mitophagy in an animal host.

items.prompt: Every BSL-4 control this record requires assumes terrestrial gravity and somewhere to put contaminated air, water and waste -- suit overpressure, airlocks, chemical showers, specialized waste disposal. Which still contain an agent in a closed-loop habitat that recycles all three?
items.rationale: Sample-return and crewed-habitat missions need containment for agents with no countermeasure, which is exactly what BSL-4 is for. But every control edge runs outward from bsl4_trait to a piece of equipment -- `requires` an airlock, a decontamination shower, specialized waste disposal; `necessitates use of` a positive pressure suit -- so the controls are named as hardware rather than as the physics they rely on, and it is the physics that does or does not transfer. Sedimentation-dependent controls behave differently in microgravity, and a shower and a waste stream that both feed a recycling loop are not disposal. As written the record cannot distinguish a control that survives the move from one that does not, because it never says what any of them do.

items.prompt: Which enzymes and metabolic routes maintain conversion at high solids?
items.rationale: One sequential HR1 reactor supports positive conversion and gas outcomes but does not isolate solids loading from vitamin, medium, mixing or adaptation changes. Metaproteomic replicates are not independent replicate reactors, and the sequence database was derived from lower-solids metagenomes. Selective enzyme perturbations, catalytic assays and route-resolved flux would test both existing arrows. AA6 enrichment motivated an oxidative/Fenton accessibility hypothesis, but ROS, iron cycling and lignin-depolymerization flux were not directly established in the inspected study; no new oxidative branch is asserted. The authors' proposed syntrophic acetate oxidation likewise remains unresolved. Canonical broad taxa are incomplete and are not a newly grounded strain roster. items.prompt: Separate gamete-cell fusion from autogamy and broader selfing.
items.rationale: Use the single-gametangium gamete-fusion sense established in the cited diatom literature. Autogamy traitmech:000622 denotes gametic-nuclear fusion in an unpaired undivided cell, without fusion of separate gametes; cytogamy traitmech:000623 concerns paired cells without nuclear exchange. Automixis is broader in Kaczmarska et al. section 5.2 and is not an exact synonym. Bagmet et al. calls automixis homothallic, whereas our existing homothallism traitmech:000609 is fungal-scoped; this usage does not make that record a parent. The parent gap is resolved by automixis traitmech:000625, whose single-meiotic-cell nuclear origin includes this operational scope. The broader terminology and mapping questions keep this discussion OPEN. Do not infer species-level disjointness or universal homozygosity, recombination rate, seasonal trigger or inability to outcross. Broader non-diatom usage and external equivalences need primary source review before expanding this operational scope.

items.prompt: Assess the functional qualifier and distinguish same-cell recovery from descendant reset.
items.rationale: Require an age-linked deficit and a measured recovery or replicative-potential reset, retaining the endpoint, age axis, comparison group, treated unit, conditions and persistence. Recovery of one function need not restore all functions, be permanent or extend lifespan. Descendant recovery must not be reported as repair of the old mother. Marker changes, lifespan extension alone, prevention without prior loss and sexual immaturity alone are insufficient. Bare cellular rejuvenation has broader source usages and is not an exact synonym. Autogamy, gametogenesis and dormancy exit are not themselves this phenotype; neither is replicative aging with functional decline. Culture age is not interchangeable with lineage age. METPO:1000059 phenotype is a conservative parent, with no reparenting of existing records or asserted external equivalence.

items.prompt: Should a short stand-alone DUF4062 protein be annotated as an NTPase because its orthogroup is labelled a NACHT NTPase?
items.rationale: Orthogroup labels such as COG5635, "Predicted NTPase, NACHT family domain", group short stand-alone DUF4062 proteins together with large multidomain relatives in which the NTP-hydrolysing NACHT domain is a separate domain adjacent to DUF4062. Automated pipelines transfer the NTPase label across that boundary. In a UniProtKB snapshot taken on 2026-10-30, a P-loop NTPase domain (IPR027417) co-occurs with DUF4062 in 2514 of 2925 proteins over 450 aa, or 85.9%, but in only 23 of 1720 proteins of 450 aa or less, or 1.3%, and NACHT itself in one. The activity reported for the domain is NAD+ hydrolysis, a different chemistry from NTP hydrolysis. This bears on how DUFMech should treat orthogroup-derived functional labels generally. It is not resolved here, and no NTPase activity has been tested for or excluded in any short member.

items.prompt: Preserve relational phenotype scope without equating all recognition or cooperation.
items.rationale: Stefanic 2015 defines conspecific discrimination, whereas Lyons 2017 explicitly extends exclusion to nearby species. The record retains that attributed extension without a universal kin threshold, obligate killing, cognition or monotonic distance-response rule. Kin recognition, allorecognition and self/nonself discrimination are not asserted as exact synonyms. An interaction phenotype is required; a recognition locus, allele match, isolated pairing or spatial assortment alone is insufficient. Recognition-allele specificity, measured relatedness proxies and genome-wide relatedness must not be conflated. METPO:1000059 phenotype is the conservative parent. Mutualism (traitmech:000041) requires reciprocal benefit; biofilm formation (traitmech:000053) is neither necessary nor sufficient. Contact-dependent outer membrane exchange (traitmech:000650) is material transfer, and its existing negative kin-discrimination evidence remains a boundary, not a parent gap. Heterokaryon incompatibility (traitmech:000606) concerns postfusion restriction and is not automatically equivalent or reparented. Predation requires trophic benefit; DNA self/nonself defense has a different target and endpoint. No organism-level disjointness is implied.

Selected thesis Methods, Results, Discussion and actual pages 69, 73, 75, 86 and 89 were inspected, not all figures, tables or raw data. Ground inoculum may include nonviable material; no killed-host control was inspected, which is not proof none exists. Table accessions identify BLAST reference strains, not experimental isolate deposits. No canonical taxa, exact external mappings, protein examples or causal graph are asserted. The measured enzyme activity is not a molecular effector identification. Metadata and notice checks were bounded; some publisher endpoints failed. Source URLs, hashes, version distinctions and native verification results are retained in the sidecar.

items.prompt: Separate osmotic migration from tolerance, kinesis and chemical specificity.

Exclude passive transport, osmotic water movement and differential growth as sole evidence. Osmokinesis is not an exact synonym, even when it contributes to spatial redistribution. Solute-specific chemotaxis can coexist with osmotaxis, as the Barros study reports; the Leslie result does not negate it universally. The local chemotaxis record imposes flagellar motor switching, so motile is used as the verified broader parent. External equivalents remain unasserted pending authority and organismal-scope checks.

items.prompt: Resolve the broader feeding hierarchy without imposing a capture mechanism or carbon-specific endpoint.
items.rationale: Feeding on living or previously dead nematodes is included; fungal killing, obligacy and starvation are not universal requirements. Mere contact, paralysis, killing, trap formation or a sequence annotation alone is insufficient. Fungal nematode-trap formation (traitmech:000718) is structural, neither necessary nor sufficient for feeding. Mycoparasitism (traitmech:000717) has fungal prey; predatory bacterium (traitmech:000054) has a bacterial actor and prey. Phagotrophy (traitmech:000628), myzocytosis (traitmech:000631) and pallium feeding (traitmech:000632) impose different uptake modes. Saprotrophy (traitmech:000055) can overlap, without organism-level disjointness. Local parasitism (traitmech:000043) inherits persistent association, not required here. Keep phenotype METPO:1000059 pending a closer feeding hierarchy; no universal carbon, nitrogen or energy contribution is specified. Bare nematophagy includes nonfungal actors and is not an exact synonym. No unverified synonyms or xrefs are asserted.

items.prompt: Review the stalk-extension endpoint and its projection-contraction parent.
items.rationale: The measured endpoint is reduced end-to-end stalk extension, not necessarily reduced contour length. Coiling is observed, not a universal geometric requirement. Require active cellular contraction; static stalk morphology, reduced developmental growth, passive bending, detachment and isometric force alone do not establish it. Stalk-induced body displacement is not cell-body contraction traitmech:000728, and the endpoint differs from rapid axopodial contraction traitmech:000682. The direct parent is cell body or cytoplasmic projection contraction traitmech:000729, by definition-based inference. Amos's publisher abstract places the spasmoneme within cytoplasm and a sheath. The stalk is composite; its whole sheath is not asserted to be cytoplasm. Neither locomotion nor a universal ATP-driven motor is required by this parent choice. No exact synonym or organism-level disjointness is asserted.

items.prompt: Retain cue-dependent preparation without conflating neighboring temporal-response traits.
items.rationale: The cue-triggered qualifier is deliberate: solely clock-driven preparation or constitutive readiness is insufficient. Evidence must link the preceding cue to preparation for a different later condition; correlated expression or cross-protection alone does not establish that interpretation. Generic stress response, stochastic bet hedging, carbon-source memory and diauxic growth are not exact synonyms, although particular observations can overlap. Neither cognition nor learning within an individual's lifetime is required; evolutionary regulatory wiring is compatible. No universal benefit, fixed delay, asymmetric response or single mechanism is required. METPO:1000731 nutrient adaptation is locally framed as chronic copiotroph/oligotroph trophic adaptation, not this cue-to-future-condition phenotype. METPO:1000059 phenotype is the conservative parent pending upstream hierarchy review. This is an organismal disposition, not a sequence feature, regulatory site or precomposed chemical-use assertion.

items.prompt: Preserve organism-level self-fertility across distinct mating mechanisms.
items.rationale: This is a reproductive phenotype, not a sequence feature or MAT-gene inventory. The operational single-spore definition does not require a uninucleate spore, both MAT idiomorphs in one nucleus, or one molecular mechanism. It does not exclude outcrossing or require universal compatibility, obligate sexuality, or self-fertility of every progeny. Distinguish self-fertility from asexual cloning, ploidy, heterokaryosis, hyphal fusion and parasexual reproduction; these are not is-a parents. PHYSIOLOGY is a filesystem category, not an ontology parent. Self-fertility and self-compatibility also have uses outside fungi; resolve their lexical scope and external phenotype/process mappings before adding synonyms or xrefs.

items.prompt: Review the withdrawal endpoint without making universal entry-time claims.

Partial withdrawal counts; permanent intactness and complete withdrawal are not required. Bacterial polar ejection traitmech:000732 releases structures externally; eukaryotic axoneme internalization traitmech:000734 involves a different apparatus. These distinctions do not imply disjoint organisms. Earlier 109J observations of externally retained filaments constrain universal early-entry claims but neither demonstrate own-periplasmic withdrawal nor establish its absence. Different strains and preparations are not pooled into one time series.

items.prompt: Refine the egg-infection hierarchy without conflating infection, feeding and hatching endpoints.

Animal pathogen METPO:1004002 is active below pathogenic to host METPO:1004000 and phenotype METPO:1000059. Its pinned organism-like wording is clarified as a phenotype in current upstream METPO; the local parent is not rewritten. Nematode egg infection does not entail mammalian pathogenicity. Xie describes this fungus as nematophagous, but the operational infection endpoint does not quantify feeding: fungal nematophagy traitmech:000719 requires consumption and also includes dead prey. It is related, not an asserted parent here. Local parasitism traitmech:000043 inherits persistent symbiosis, which is not required. No organism-level disjointness, obligacy, exclusive host stage or universal host range is asserted. Bare egg parasitism does not specify the fungal actor and is not an exact synonym.

Keep historical assay observations separate from this current catalog state; loss alone does not establish engineering. PLY182g provenance remains unresolved here. No universal silicon requirement, ploidy restriction, growth dependence or protective function is inferred. Separate mineral deposition, transport, secretion and covering integrity before adding causal edges. A protein mechanism needs direct functional evidence and taxon-paired accessions; sequence features alone are insufficient. Mechanism is deferred, not claimed absent.

items.prompt: Resolve an exact external ontology class for lysine decarboxylase activity before adding a TraitRecord xref.
items.rationale: GO:0008923 carries the same lysine decarboxylase activity label but denotes the enzyme molecular function rather than the organism-level lysine decarboxylase production phenotype, so it is appropriate as a causal-node grounding rather than an equivalent TraitRecord xref.

items.prompt: Resolve native force generation beyond the observed Sfi1 perturbation outcomes.
items.rationale: Fixed-state morphology, localization and knockdown do not uniquely determine a molecular motor cycle.

items.prompt: Assess remaining upstream terminology for the explicitly decline-qualified phenotype.
items.rationale: Replicative age follows a cell or inherited cell lineage across successive divisions; culture age alone is not that measurement. Use age-resolved performance or mortality risk, not merely a finite lifespan, old-pole identity, endpoint death, cumulative survival loss or an old/new sibling difference. A decline can approach a plateau; continuous worsening until death is not required. The record uses the functional-decline sense of aging, while Horkai et al. 2023 explicitly distinguish senescence from broader replicative ageing. The label is now explicitly qualified as replicative aging with functional decline (#1891); bare replicative aging is not asserted as an exact synonym. Upstream review should assess remaining terminology and hierarchy choices; no external xref is asserted. Chronological survival in nondividing cultures, population-wide clonal senescence and irreversible mammalian cell-cycle arrest are not equated with this phenotype. The existing gram-variable culture_aging node denotes stationary-phase conditions and is not an exact grounding target. METPO:1000059 phenotype is the conservative broader class; no existing record is reparented.

items.prompt: How should the native C. zeina CTB7-pseudogene locus and complemented production experiment be represented separately?
items.rationale: PMID:28535078 reports cercosporin in one C. zeina transformant complemented with full-length C. zeae-maydis CTB7 under nitrogen-limited/light conditions. It reports lack of native in-vitro production in the studied context and only proposes a structural variant during maize infection. KY656140.1 is the partial native CTB region with a CTB7 pseudogene, from deposited isolate CMW25467, not the complemented construct. The LOTUS occurrence cites the same study and requires the same experimental-context audit; occurrence and production remain distinct claims. The publisher full text was inaccessible. This qualification does not prove species-wide absence, upgrade SOURCE_ASSERTION or CLUSTER_UNSTATED, or change the compound-origin class to ENGINEERED. Claim-level context or withholding requires further source-pinned curation.

items.prompt: Add primary literature evidence for metabolic versatility, regulatory network plasticity, and broad resource-utilization pathways in a cited exemplar taxon before constructing causal_graphs.
items.rationale: The current record carries two high-level ecological classification snippets (DOI:10.1093/femsec/fiaa240; DOI:10.1038/s41559-023-02027-7) contrasting niche breadth in generalists vs specialists without molecular mechanism quotes or a canonical example.

items.prompt: Does community composition mediate the substrate-specific endpoints?
items.rationale: All three positive observations and the existing direction remain. The complete primary main text supports substrate selection, CMC core composition and xylan caproate accumulation, while explicitly relying on inferred metabolic functions. The study does not isolate necessary member contributions or directly measure interspecies flux. Preserve the earlier hydrogen-flux and amplicon-scope discussions; no new pairwise mechanism or niche-partitioning classification is added.

items.prompt: Resolve preparation-dependent contributions of stellate contraction to flagellar excision.
items.rationale: Published results disagree, and the perturbations affect multiple assemblies.

items.prompt: Resolve exact source-neutral groundings and boundaries for funis tubulins, dense rods, epiplasm-associated anchors and any additional funis-associated proteins.
items.rationale: The funis is a Giardia microtubule array associated with dense rods and the epiplasm, but this pass did not identify exact molecular components for those associated structures.

items.prompt: Resolve exact source-neutral InterPro, Pfam, or NCBIfam groundings for the yeast TORC2 Tor2, Avo1, Avo2, Tsc11/Avo3, Lst8, Bit61, Slm1 and Slm2 subunit classes.
items.rationale: This first TORC2 record names the yeast protein constituents but leaves family grounding unset until exact source-neutral boundaries for shared TOR/Lst8 classes and TORC2-specific classes are reviewed.

items.prompt: Keep stiffness-directed migration distinct from other mechanical responses.
items.rationale: The class is polarity-neutral: positive and negative responses are directions along the stiffness gradient, not different stimuli. Isomursu et al. (DOI:10.1038/s41563-022-01294-2) support this terminology in mammalian cells, not negative microbial durotaxis. Both microbial studies here report stiff-side migration; no opposite microbial response is inferred. Speed changes on uniform substrates, passive displacement and differential growth alone are insufficient. Contact-guided polarized growth in thigmotropism (traitmech:000594) is a different response. Do not infer durotaxis from a friction gradient, surface topography or remote substrate deformation without direct evidence for stiffness-directed migration. Mechanotaxis is broader, not an exact synonym. QuickGO returned zero durotaxis hits on 2026-10-04; other external equivalences remain unverified. No xref or synonym is inferred.

items.prompt: Extend BEST1 gating and permeability contexts while preserving construct, orientation and assay differences.
items.rationale: Purified current and coupled-flux effects do not directly resolve every gating microstep or establish a universal family mechanism. The tested truncated region maps exactly despite full-length differences between historical and current references.

items.prompt: Distinguish transport machinery and neighboring PAS components from IPOD constituents.
items.rationale: Recruitment defects, pulldown association and partial colocalization do not establish stable composition.

items.prompt: This record is labelled 'compound 7', which is a label from the cited paper's own numbering rather than a compound name. Resolve a name from the literature or a structure registry.

attaches_to: ecological_interactions#CL95 colonization and rhizosphere enzyme response
items.prompt: Which CL95 member strains and secreted metabolites directly suppress Ilyonectria robusta or drive the measured ginseng growth-promotion and rhizosphere enzyme phenotypes?
items.rationale: Tian et al. 2026 connected CL95 to strong pathogen suppression, plant growth promotion, tissue/rhizosphere colonization, and soil-enzyme responses, but did not assign the community phenotypes to a specific member or molecule. Plate antagonism does not isolate resource competition, and improved host growth does not measure reciprocal bacterial fitness. Selective-CFU recovery, plate nutrient-screen zones, soil enzyme activities, defense-gene expression and amplicon correlations were measured in distinct assays; they do not selectively establish a colonization, nutrient-flux, induced-systemic-resistance or microbiome-recruitment mediation chain. In particular, defense transcription is positive host-response evidence, not a pathway-blockade test of necessity. The suppression-to-growth arrow is removed because it encodes joint treatment outcomes rather than isolated mediation. Resolve strain-specific marker readout, relevant perturbations and the abstract/main-text soil-enzyme percentage discrepancy before assigning exact member effects or new causal branches.

items.prompt: Resolve an exact source-neutral protein-family identifier for fumarate reductase subunit B before replacing its reviewed-label-only component row.
items.rationale: InterPro IPR004489 covers succinate dehydrogenase and fumarate reductase iron-sulfur proteins, so this record grounds exact FrdA, FrdC, and FrdD families while leaving FrdB ungrounded until a FrdB-specific family is verified.

items.prompt: Resolve pAgo subfamily boundaries, accessory-protein requirements, and substrate breadth before minting narrower long-pAgo or APAZ-associated defense children.
items.rationale: SPARTA and DdmDE support prokaryotic Argonaute defense systems as a reusable genomics family, and DefenseFinder models a pAgo namespace with long pAgo, SPARTA, and optional APAZ-associated profiles. This parent does not yet resolve whether every DefenseFinder pAgo submodel has the same plasmid or phage substrate range, whether standalone APAZ-associated profiles are exact children, or which native-host examples support each subfamily.

items.prompt: Which individual products and experimental contexts belong to the sixteen generic carotenoid source concepts?
items.rationale: All sixteen MIBiG concepts attach a generic carotenoid label to the same C46H90O6 glycoside (PubChem CID446841). The encoded graph has one nonaromatic carbon-carbon double bond. The cited studies concern distinct products: PMID11432736 identifies C50 decaprenoxanthin in Corynebacterium glutamicum, while PMID18820900 describes a C30 pathway in Halobacillus halophilus. Matching source registry keys cannot establish all sixteen producer/locus joins or the nine LOTUS occurrences for this exact structure. PMID11200234 also requires explicit engineered-expression context rather than assuming detectable native production. Re-adjudicate each concept and occurrence from exact primary structures and experiments, preserving unresolved stereochemistry. No replacement graph or blanket evidence-grade upgrade is justified here.

items.prompt: Resolve exact source-neutral groundings for the Sm ring and U4atac-specific protein families that form the U4atac snRNP.
items.rationale: The first GO:0005690 record captures U4atac snRNA and the GO-defined Sm ring at coarse granularity. Individual spliceosomal Sm proteins and U4atac-specific protein-family boundaries should be resolved before splitting this inventory.

items.prompt: How reproducible is wax-ester coproduction and how much of the yeast benefit is specifically mediated by detoxification?
items.rationale: Primary results support faster inhibitor conversion and higher lactic acid productivity, not a higher lactic acid yield or neutral ADP1 fitness. Wax esters were reliably quantified in only one of four coculture replicates, and residual feedstock must be distinguished from yeast-produced carbon. The authors' facultative-mutualism interpretation does not demonstrate obligate dependence. Preserve all three nodes and both PARTIAL directions; no new culture, strain-design or optimization instructions are added.

items.prompt: Resolve the exact mapping between DefenseFinder NLR_like_bNACHT01 and NLR_like_bNACHT09 profiles and the experimentally tested bNACHT proteins, natural host breadth, phage triggers, and bNACHT effector mechanisms before minting narrower bNACHT subtype traits.
items.rationale: Kibby et al. support bacterial NACHT proteins as NLR-related phage-defense proteins and DefenseFinder models NLR_like_bNACHT01 and NLR_like_bNACHT09 as single-profile NLR-family subsystems. This first system-level record leaves profile-to-assayed-protein correspondence and subtype-specific trigger and effector mechanisms unresolved.

items.prompt: Resolve an exact external ontology class for organism-level tetrathionate respiration before adding a TraitRecord xref.
items.rationale: The pinned METPO snapshot has no active organism-level class for tetrathionate respiration. Candidate EC, Rhea, and protein-family terms for tetrathionate reductase or the TtrA/TtrB/TtrC complex are narrower than the whole-organism anaerobic respiration phenotype.

items.prompt: Resolve GAPS2 natural host breadth, BRCT-domain activity, phage trigger specificity, and exact GAPS2__GAPS2 profile-to-protein correspondence before minting narrower GAPS2 mechanism traits.
items.rationale: Mahata et al. support GAPS2 as a GMT-encoded anti-phage defense system that protects E. coli against P1-vir and lambda-vir when expressed from a Vibrio parahaemolyticus locus, and DefenseFinder represents GAPS2 as a single-profile system. Natural host breadth, BRCT-domain activity, the phage trigger, and exact profile-to-protein correspondence remain unresolved.

items.prompt: Resolve exact source-neutral protein components that form the 7SK snRNP.
items.rationale: The first GO:0120259 record captures 7SK RNA, which defines the 7SK snRNP in GO. Protein-family and subcomplex boundaries should be resolved before expanding this component list.

items.prompt: Resolve family-wide mechanisms and classify borderline loci.
items.rationale: Short denotes the phylogenetic and structural LmuB family, not an arbitrary amino-acid cutoff or an isolated short protein. LmuC-loss clade S and effector-domain-loss clade O preclude requiring one universal three-component effector architecture. Type I/II component classifications and effector names are not exact synonyms for this family. HNH's explicitly short-form definition supports its new parent; SMEK's unresolved long-profile call prevents the same inference. Other table-defined subtypes require their own scope review before reparenting. The Vc-Cap4 mechanism already described on the Lamassu parent is not assumed universal across short-family effectors, so no duplicate or universal mechanism graph is asserted here. A registry Hypothetical label must not be equated with clade O's effector-domain loss without explicit evidence. The LmuC-loss architecture is now represented separately by traitmech:000573 Lamassu type I system. The paper identifies clade S as type I; clade O's effector-domain loss remains a distinct question. The new component class is not treated as a synonym for this whole length family, and its broader phylogenetic distribution is left open rather than inferred from one clade. Existing hierarchy and mechanism scope are unchanged.

items.prompt: Which direct substrates and intermediates are consumed by each of R. opacus DSM 43250, P. putida KT2440, and Pseudomonas sp. VLB120 during optimized PPOW degradation?
items.rationale: The source proposes an alkane, aromatic, and solvent-tolerance division of labor after process optimization but explicitly says the specific mechanism remains unclear; resolving the gap could turn the community-level niche-partitioning model into direct member-metabolite assertions.

items.prompt: Verify strain and life-stage provenance before adding examples or mechanisms.

Inspect full studies and relevant supplements, distinguish spatial observations from temporal-shock measurements and model interpretations, and resolve taxon-paired protein accessions before adding molecular causal graphs. Verify unperturbed natural strain provenance and NCBI identity before adding canonical examples; promastigote observations must retain their life-stage restriction. A NONMECHANISTIC graph must not bypass those requirements.

items.prompt: Resolve an exact source-neutral grounding for the lipid constituent of the cis-Golgi network membrane.

items.prompt: This structure is reported by more than one MIBiG entry: BGC0000136, BGC0000137. Confirm they describe the same compound rather than an upstream cross-reference error.

items.prompt: Resolve DS-15 native host breadth, exact profile-to-protein mapping, DS-15A/DS-15B/DS-15C component activities, sensitive-phage breadth, exact AAA family ATPase and DUF6988 chemistry, and rule-level DefenseFinder criteria before minting narrower DS-15 mechanism children.

items.rationale: The four-family list is incomplete and must not be interpreted as the universal composition of every A-C linker.

items.prompt: Keep the whole array distinct from its organizing center and other microtubule networks.
items.rationale: Parsed checks over 906 existing records and hidden/ignored-inclusive name, accession and citation searches found no whole-array duplicate. GO:1990295 exactly denotes the array, with parent GO:0110165, part-of GO:0015630 and has-part GO:0000923. The has-part existential is not inverted into universal center part-of array. OTHER describes the multi-filament system, not a single filament or fixed stoichiometric complex. ePAA and lPAA are equatorial and longitudinal portions, not early/late arrays or exact whole-array synonyms. Spindle, interphase arrays, individual microtubules and microtubule ends remain distinct.

items.prompt: Resolve Belenos phage triggers and effector outputs before minting narrower Belenos mechanism children.
items.rationale: Darracq et al. and DefenseFinder support Belenos as a named anti-phage system with a VCA0457 profile, but the trigger, molecular substrate, antiviral effector output, and subtype-specific mechanism are not resolved enough here to assert a narrower mechanistic child trait.

items.prompt: Resolve cord-specific centrin paralogues, scaffold constituents and selective assembly requirements.

The 2013 primary paper was not retrieved; current graph edges adopt UniProt annotations only. items.prompt: Resolve source inconsistencies and strain provenance before adding rates, examples or causal mechanisms.
items.rationale: Xu Supplementary Table 1 reports a 30-hour mean of 38% for replicates 38%, 33% and 33%, whose arithmetic mean is about 34.7%. This discrepancy is preserved, not silently corrected. Its main Methods sample-level wording is less precise than the supplement's individual-egg penetration criterion. No rates or infection threshold are curated. Xie's conserved appressorium genes also occur in fungi lacking that structure; neither gene inventory nor differential expression establishes this trait or a protein-resolved mechanism. No causal graph, protein example or canonical taxon is asserted without further authority and strain-provenance checks. Microscopy and source-designated infection are not tracer measurements of nutrient flux. No field efficacy or safety claim follows. Source hashes, inspected figures/supplement, actual snippet verdicts and bounded notice checks are retained in the verification sidecar; no comprehensive correction/retraction clearance is claimed. Both counted primary experiments concern Purpureocillium lilacinum (JZD02 and 36-1). The fungal actor class is not evidence that this phenotype was experimentally demonstrated across fungal species; additional species require their own evidence.

items.prompt: Distinguish the Stentor myoneme system from homonymous and neighboring assemblies.
items.rationale: A shared protein or historical name does not establish structural equivalence.

items.prompt: Discriminate gravity signaling from touch and coincident development.
items.rationale: Bending observations do not resolve a complete molecular mechanism. Vacuolization can coincide with development; touch-induced ion fluxes do not establish gravity-triggered channel activity. The 2004 abstract compares strains with and without crystals but does not identify a universal sole gravity sensor. Inspect its full text and resolve eligible taxon-paired protein accessions before adding a mechanistic graph. Do not use NONMECHANISTIC to bypass grounding requirements or transfer Chara signaling to fungi.

items.prompt: Leave PriC and DnaG out of the GO:1990158 DnaB-DnaC-DnaT-PriA-PriB complex.

items.prompt: Resolve VP1840 native host breadth, exact single-component activity, profile-to-protein mapping, homolog boundary, full phage breadth, molecular output, and rule-level DefenseFinder criteria before minting narrower VP1840 mechanism children.
items.rationale: Getz et al. support VP1840 as one of nine RIMD 2210633 integron-encoded cassettes whose cloned expression reduced phage plaquing, Supplementary Tables 8, 9, and 12 map VP1840 to VP_RS08920/Vp1840, WP_005483293.1, VSV105-vp1840, and phage-plating fold changes, and Supplementary Data 1 reports PSI-BLAST homologs. The pinned DefenseFinder HMM inventory records one VP1840 custom profile row. The pinned rules table has no VP1840 row, and the first-pass record does not resolve native host breadth, complete phage breadth, direct profile-to-protein correspondence, molecular output, or endogenous activity.

items.prompt: Add primary microbial literature evidence for PhoA/PhoX alkaline phosphatase catalysis (EC 3.1.3.1), phosphate-ester hydrolysis products, and PhoBR regulation before constructing causal_graphs.
items.rationale: The current record carries one constitutive-expression snippet and one API ZYM profile list (DOI:10.1128/JB.185.16.4983-4991.2003, DOI:10.1155/2021/8888641) without distinct catalytic reaction/product quotes for a multi-edge graph.

items.prompt: Which native-community changes mediate the measured pepper growth response?

Preserve the four-member taxonomy and earlier label repairs. No new topology is supported by the inspected experimental comparisons.

items.prompt: Keep repeat measurements separate from map dimensions and assembly hypotheses.

items.prompt: Resolve AliA catalytic sufficiency and AliB processing chemistry without collapsing substrate-specific observations.

items.prompt: Does group III diazotrophy supply nitrogen to other biofilm members?
items.rationale: The primary isolation abstract supports a free-living nitrogen-fixing organism. The biofilm proteomic abstract reports nitrogen-fixation proteins were not identified. Neither accessible primary abstract resolves nitrogen release, uptake by another member or the asserted succession/keystone mechanism. Remove the transfer node without treating nondetection as proof of no capacity. Complete main texts for these sources were not accessible in this pass; non-graph roles remain issue1764.

items.prompt: Resolve Lamassu-Cap4 nuclease phage triggers, native hosts, Cap4 nuclease substrates, LmuC usage, and profile-to-activity criteria before minting enzyme, trigger, or component children.

This first-pass record leaves exact Cap4 nuclease substrates, LmuC requirement, native hosts, phage triggers, cell-death output, profile-to-activity criteria, and the relationship between the DefenseFinder _II row and the structurally characterized Lamassu Vc-Cap4 branch unresolved.

items.prompt: Resolve exact 90S preribosome RNA, ribosomal-protein, U3-associated-protein, 40S-processing-factor and SSU-processome boundaries.

The exact source-neutral RNA and protein-family groundings, plus the distinction between the GO:0030686 90S preribosome and the related GO:0032040 small-subunit processome sibling, need a narrower literature-backed curation pass.

items.prompt: Add strain-matched UniProtKB protein_examples for the Shewanella oneidensis MR-1 SO1427-SO1432 (DmsEFABGH) extracellular DMSO reductase complex so dmso_respiration_reductase_sketch can be promoted from NONMECHANISTIC to MECHANISTIC.

items.prompt: The article body states that Text S12 contains details of the Pseudomonas_sp1 and A. pyrenoidosa co-culture experiment; those supplementary details should be inspected to recover the exact medium, inoculum, volume, and exposure groups for the pairwise assay.
items.rationale: The main article cleanly establishes Pseudomonas_sp1 as the selected partner and reports the 13-day response, but it points cultivation details for that follow-up pairwise assay to Text S12.

items.prompt: Resolve exact source-neutral groundings and component boundaries for the prospore membrane leading-edge coat subunits.
items.rationale: The initial record treats the leading-edge coat as one reviewed-label-only constituent and records Saccharomyces SSP1, ADY3 and DON1 as gene-symbol metadata. Exact family groundings for individual Ssp1, Ady3, Don1 and Irc10 components, and the boundary between stable coat proteins and Spo20/Sso1 fusion machinery, need a focused curation pass.

items.rationale: The primary article reported significant proteomic and metabolomic changes in the Cd-stressed coculture, but explicitly framed ABC transporters and Ohr-family peroxiredoxin as hypotheses rather than validated causal factors.

attaches_to: ecological_interactions#Butyric Acid Support of Butanol Production
items.prompt: How much of solventogenesis and partner dynamics is mediated by acid transfer, pH and resource competition?
items.rationale: PMID:25023325 supports sugar supply, in-situ acid formation and measured solvent production, and experimentally compares inoculation timing, ratio and pH-control duration. The full primary Results/Discussion leave molecular competition/cooperation unresolved. RNA/cDNA-based 16S proportions are not direct cell counts. Partner-resolved flux, selective acid perturbations with matched pH, and independent population quantification would distinguish these contributions. Butyrate provision does not itself establish a causal arrow to upstream saccharification.

items.rationale: This first GO-backed record captures the SPB-associated SIN/MEN complex without treating lineage-specific protein names as conserved component families or guessing InterPro, Pfam, NCBIfam, UniProtKB, or Complex Portal groundings.

items.prompt: Resolve an exact source-neutral grounding for the lipid constituent of the mitochondrial inner boundary membrane.

items.prompt: Resolve natural strain provenance and column-specific mechanisms.
items.rationale: Live NCBI https://eutils.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/entrez/eutils/efetch.fcgi?db=taxonomy&id=47266 resolves Dactylellina cionopaga at species rank, with Monacrosporium cionopagum and Dactylella cionopaga synonyms. It does not identify YMF1.01472 as a strain accession or establish its origin. The 2020 paper's cionopagum spelling and experimental strain must be reconciled before a canonical example is added; do not conflate strains across these papers. Formation, adhesion, capture, penetration and digestion are separate endpoints; formation alone does not guarantee capture in every condition. Protein-resolved causal graphs require column-specific perturbation/complementation evidence and taxon-paired accessions. Sequence features and expression correlations are not validated phenotype predictors. No mechanism is transferred from nets, knobs or rings; mechanism is deferred, not claimed absent.

items.prompt: No producer claim is written from BGC0000199, which gives NCBITaxon:77133 (uncultured bacterium — shared by every unplaced bacterium), because the taxon names no single organism. The cluster is kept: a characterized locus is an origin assertion whether or not its host has a name, and for a compound from an uncultured symbiont that is the honest state. Name the producer if the primary literature does.
Keep the central plaque distinct from the inner and outer spindle-pole-body plaques.

attaches_to: ecological_interactions#Fe(III) Reduction Coupled to Organic Acid Oxidation
ecological_interactions#Candidate Iron-Reduction Suppression of Acetoclastic Methanogenesis
items.prompt: Do direct redox and carbon-flux measurements confirm iron cycling and methane suppression?
items.rationale: PMID:37996661 reports genomic abundance changes from thaw incubations, not resolved iron/carbon flux. Oxygen conditions were inferred despite nitrogen purging. Acetate perturbations, methane production measurements and partner-specific iron transfer are needed to distinguish the proposed mechanisms. GO:0006826 describes ion transport rather than the redox reactions curated here.

attaches_to: ecological_interactions#Two-Site Field Disease Suppression and Yield Increase
items.prompt: Which metabolites and colonization dynamics connect Bacillus G12/Y4/X25 co-cultivation to tobacco root signaling, pathogen inhibition, and persistence in tobacco rhizosphere or endophytic niches?
items.rationale: The reviewed cache contains selected methods/results/discussion, not independent complete full text. Plate inhibition, Salkowski output, glasshouse disease/root activity and estimated middle-leaf field yield are distinct endpoints. No fixed duration, number of divisions, benefit, particular sugar, or molecular mechanism is required. Genetic adaptation, immune memory, chemotactic temporal sensing, stress priming and stochastic bet hedging are not equivalent. METPO:1000731 nutrient adaptation is a trophic-type class locally framed as the chronic copiotroph/oligotroph axis; diauxic growth denotes sequential nutrient use, and generalist/specialist describe niche breadth. Cytogamy's existing 1979 evidence supports same-parent meiotic origin despite cell pairing; cytoplasmic exchange is not nuclear outcrossing. Same-clone mating after different meioses is insufficient. items.prompt: Review a closer multicellular morphology parent and branching terminology.
items.rationale: Use phenotype METPO:1000059 below quality METPO:1000188. Branched shaped METPO:1000687 concerns lateral branches in cell shape, not necessarily this arrangement of trichomes; no subclass or equivalence is asserted. The Golubic 1996 definition authority includes bundle partitioning as well as lateral protrusion. The Scytonema example demonstrates the latter and must not narrow the whole class. Necridium formation traitmech:000674 describes a separation cell, not all false branches. Hormogonium formation traitmech:000651 describes dispersal filaments, not the branching topology. Obsolete cell-arrangement METPO terms redirect to flagellar arrangement, which is not a suitable parent here. No exact synonyms, xrefs, SSSOM mappings or organism-level disjointness are asserted; historical pseudo-branch usages need review. The label is qualified as cyanobacterial false branching because the directly read English scientific abstract of Nesterenko et al. (1980), PMID:6782438 (https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/6782438/), uses false branching for growth of separated cell ends in the organism historically named Brevibacterium helvolum ATCC 19239. That distinct usage is not evidence for cyanobacterial trichome development. Its full text and modern taxonomic identity were not inspected. No unqualified exact synonym or cross-taxon mechanism is asserted. See review issue #1821.

Motility of both gametes and external fertilization describe the canonical example, not universal requirements. The definition compares gamete types, not incidental size variation within a type, vegetative-versus-gamete size, or mating compatibility. Oogamy traitmech:000621 now supplies the size-dimorphic child with large nonmotile female gametes. Its evidence explicitly preserves nonmotile male exceptions rather than imposing a universal motility convention. Verify lexical/external mappings and a narrower reproductive parent before adding them. Kaczmarska et al. (2017), DOI:10.1371/journal.pone.0181413, also use physiological/behavioural anisogamy for approximately equal-sized gametes in diatoms. Ectoine and glycine betaine both enable osmotic stress tolerance here, but trehalose is wired instead to environmental stress tolerance -- a node with no outgoing edge. Is that split a real distinction, or does trehalose belong on the osmotic route too?
items.rationale: Because environmental_stress_tolerance has no outgoing edge, nothing downstream depends on trehalose at all: this record currently predicts the trait's osmotolerance from two systems and leaves the third dangling. Either reading has a consequence. If trehalose does serve osmotic tolerance, a genome carrying only trehalose scores as non-osmotolerant when it is not, which is exactly the inference anything reading habitat range off gene content would make. If the split is real -- trehalose for desiccation and thermal stress rather than osmolarity -- then the dangling node needs its own edge onward to the trait. The second question, whether the two routes that do converge are redundant or condition-partitioned, rides along on the same experiment: their costs differ sharply, since de novo ectoine synthesis is carbon-expensive where betaine uptake is cheap given a precursor.

Nondegradative membrane repair or ejection using autophagy machinery is not sufficient. Extracellular uptake and ordinary phagolysosomal digestion alone do not distinguish autophagy. items.prompt: Keep the cross-level mating phenotype distinct from sequence inventory.
items.rationale: The unit is a mating system or cross with differently organized partners, not a standalone locus or a species-wide assertion about either parental strain. Three poles across the pair do not mean three mating types or three independent factors in each genome. This differs from the uniform single-factor and two-factor systems in traitmech:000616 and traitmech:000615, and from recombination-permitting chromosomal colocation in traitmech:000617. Heterothallic source framing does not make this a universal separate-partner dependence subclass of traitmech:000610; progeny can differ in self-fertility. Use released phenotype METPO:1000059 in record and proposal pending narrower relational-phenotype hierarchy review. PHYSIOLOGY is a filesystem category. No disjointness, fixed fertility ratio, natural prevalence or mandatory evolutionary trajectory is asserted. Resolve lexical and external equivalences before synonyms or xrefs.

items.prompt: Distinguish functional self-fertility from co-occurring MAT sequences.
items.rationale: This narrows operational homothallism (traitmech:000609) and agrees with the older evidence note's primary-homothallism umbrella placement. Like pseudohomothallism (traitmech:000612), it includes single-founder self-fertility, but combines determinants within one genome rather than packaging compatible nuclei in a spore. Mating-type switching (traitmech:000611) and same-type outcrossing within unisexual reproduction (traitmech:000613) do not alone imply that operational phenotype; their broader phenotype parents are not inconsistent with this narrower placement. MAT inventory alone is insufficient, as the parent's Chromocrea evidence illustrates. Do not require linked loci, one domain architecture, every MAT gene's indispensability, fixed spore counts or absence of outcrossing. These capabilities are not asserted disjoint. Resolve true-homothallism terminology and external mappings before adding synonyms or xrefs. PHYSIOLOGY is a filesystem category; the standalone METPO proposal uses released phenotype METPO:1000059 pending acceptance of homothallism METPO:1056300, not an unlabeled placeholder parent.

items.prompt: Distinguish membrane-bound uptake from neighboring capabilities.
items.rationale: This is the microbial cell's uptake phenotype, not a host response, a sequence feature or intracellular trafficking alone. Surface adsorption, passive diffusion, transporter entry, open membrane invaginations and autophagy alone are insufficient. Pinocytosis traitmech:000635 and phagocytosis traitmech:000627 entail this scope; macropinocytosis traitmech:000634 remains below pinocytosis. items.prompt: Two edges reach genome reduction here: confined habitat through metabolic gene loss, and the trait itself, whose description bundles drift in as `with small Ne`. The nodes that would give drift a mechanism -- transmission bottleneck, limited recombination -- connect to neither. Should they feed the drift edge, and which mechanism dominates?
items.rationale: The record asserts both mechanisms but at different resolutions, which is what makes them impossible to weigh. Drift arrives bundled into a trait-level edge as a parenthetical -- `with small Ne` inside a description -- while selection is spelled out as a two-step path through metabolic_gene_loss. transmission_bottleneck and limited_recombination attach to each other and to nothing else, so the drift claim has no mechanism under it, and host_symbiont_aa_complementarity -> nutritional_compensation is likewise its own disconnected pair, so compensation is not wired into reduction either. The two predict opposite loss spectra -- drift removes genes roughly regardless of function, compensation removes exactly the genes whose products the host supplies -- so until they are stated at the same resolution the graph cannot say what a newly sequenced symbiont will have lost, which is most of what a reduction model is for.

The 2025 control cadence, 2026 cycloheximide timing and electrical-control locators remain unresolved source discrepancies. Retained public PDFs and author manuscripts are not verified equivalent to current corrected publisher versions. Bounded MED/Crossref checks are not proof of notice absence. No causal graph, exact synonym, external equivalence or species-wide phenotype is asserted. Source access challenges and caption discrepancies are retained in the source-verification sidecar.

items.prompt: Keep gravity-relative swimming distinct from settling and neighboring traits.
items.rationale: Positive and negative gravitaxis are directional cases, not a requirement that all cells always swim upward. Passive settling alone and speed changes alone do not establish this trait. The definition does not require an active gravity receptor: powered swimming and physical orientation can coexist. Gyrotaxis (traitmech:000583) specifies a gravity-viscous torque mechanism, not an exact synonym or a disjoint phenotype. No new subsumption axiom between them is asserted without reviewing both scopes. QuickGO resolved active GO:0042332 gravitaxis on 2026-10-04, including geotaxis as an exact lexical synonym. It denotes a biological process rather than this organismal disposition; keep it out of equivalent xrefs and resolve any mapping separately.

GO:0001410 was resolved through QuickGO: it is a biological process and its survival/endogenous-formation wording also needs scope review. Leave exact synonyms and xrefs unset rather than asserting equivalence. The four obsolete METPO chlamydospore terms are material classes, not active organismal phenotypes.

items.prompt: Keep gravity-guided growth separate from swimming and passive motion.
items.rationale: The class includes positive or negative directional growth without requiring both in one organism or condition. It is not gravitaxis (swimming orientation), gravikinesis (propulsion-speed change), passive settling, flotation or sagging, or gravity-dependent growth rate alone. The Phycomyces evidence here is negative. Resolve phenotype-level external equivalences before adding xrefs or synonyms.

items.prompt: Resolve strain, assay and source gaps before assigning canonical taxa or molecular mechanisms.
items.rationale: The QS45 strain-table gap and WNC032 figure-label conflict remain unresolved. The 2015 scientific abstract was read directly, but full text was not. The 2017 scientific abstract and IMPORTANCE summary were distinguished; the corrected excerpt is from the scientific abstract, not IMPORTANCE. Selected supplemental spreadsheet checks are not raw-image reanalysis or a statistical replication; supplementary EPS figures remain unread. Bounded MED, PLOS and NLM metadata checks are not exhaustive clearance of corrections or retractions; some publisher routes were inaccessible. No canonical taxa, exact external mappings, protein examples or causal graph are asserted. Allele-specific adhesion in engineered systems requires separate provenance and mechanism review, not inference of natural species-wide possession. Trophic type METPO:1000631 is locally defined by carbon, energy and electron-donor sources, heterotrophic METPO:1000644 by organic carbon, and mixotrophic METPO:1000652 by dual carbon use. This broader nutrient-acquisition mode does not prescribe a carbon source or require photosynthesis, so retain phenotype METPO:1000059 pending review of a closer nutritional-mode hierarchy. Nutrient adaptation METPO:1000731 concerns nutrient regimes, not specifically particle feeding. Do not equate phagotrophy with phagocytosis, mixotrophy, bacterivory or the bacteria-only predatory-bacterium class. Extracellular digestion without particle ingestion is outside this definition. No unverified synonym or process-level ontology xref is asserted.

items.prompt: How much wet-up mortality and respiratory carbon flux are caused by viruses?
items.rationale: Resolve burst size, genome-length conversion, extraction efficiency, persistent particles and the assumed six bacterial 16S copies per cell before assigning a fixed mortality fraction. The Results and Discussion give slightly different lower bounds, both below 1%; no equation or analysis-code reimplementation is claimed. Separate early osmotic mortality from later viral effects. Genomic lifestyle markers do not exclude nonintegrating temperate infections, and coarse host predictions do not identify every infected strain. Direct viral perturbations and carbon tracing are needed for the proposed CO2 mediation. Abstract and main-body richness summaries use different time windows, which need not be contradictory. Preserve all positive time-course evidence while retaining these uncertainty labels; non-graph metadata is not recertified.

items.rationale: Retain oxygen-regime selection of guild composition, but remove the cross-study arrow to the separate two-methanotroph model. The 2015 microcosms infer carbon coupling without identifying the mediator or reciprocal benefit; nitrogen-metabolism explanations are hypotheses. The 2020 model reports Methylomonas-to-Methylobacter formaldehyde transfer under imposed synthetic ratios, not the sediment ratio, and environmental CO2 export. Do not confuse the two methanotrophs with the methanotroph/methylotroph guild pair. Nutrient-rich dominance and formaldehyde-export statements conflict internally, tracked in #1554. Full main bodies were read, but no original figures, S4 workbook, SBML models or executable solutions were audited; the public supplemental endpoint failed HTTP500. #1553 tracks the Methylosarcina genus/species mismatch and other taxonomy/metadata. Omit that misgrounded species from explicit participants rather than silently validating it; the resulting connectivity warning is an unresolved roster defect, not grounds to invent an edge.

items.prompt: Resolve HamC function and type-II mechanisms beyond heterologous defense assays.
items.rationale: Type II denotes the HamABC locus architecture, not a HamC hit alone, a source database row or a fixed phage-protection phenotype. Type-I DNA-damage sensing and DNA-cleavage mechanisms are not generalized to this class; HamC's biochemical role and necessity remain unresolved by these sources. No causal mechanism graph or unverified protein accession is asserted. Native-host assays and accession-resolved functional evidence remain desirable. DefenseFinder and PADLOC have different component-count rules; inspect complete locus context before converting calls into trait assertions. Component absence cannot be inferred from a failed hit or incomplete assembly. Type I remains a separate discovery lead, and coexisting loci would not make organism-level type-I and type-II possession traits disjoint. The type-I lead is now represented by traitmech:000575 Hachiman type I system for the literature-defined HamC-lacking HamAB architecture. This does not imply organism-level disjointness, turn missing detector hits into absence evidence, or transfer type-I chemistry to type II. HamC function and type-II mechanisms remain unresolved.

This first-pass record therefore does not resolve a reusable DefenseFinder profile model, exact accession-level protein examples, the breadth of TagI-like systems across natural hosts, or the complete set of natural modified-cytosine sequence contexts.

Its graded-formate results for the exact S. fumaroxidans-M. formicicum coculture are curated under the Exogenous Formate Dosage environmental factor, and its FDH downregulation result on the Propionate Oxidation interaction. Two cautions came out of that ingestion: (a) the paper runs an anaerobic-sludge system ALONGSIDE the coculture, and sludge-only results (e.g. Acetobacterium homoacetogenesis rising with formate dose) must not be attributed to this two-member consortium; (b) the dose response is non-monotonic - 30 mM recovers in the later stage - so it is NOT a simple ">=30 mM inhibits" threshold.
Still open: carrier apportionment between H2 and formate for the M. formicicum pair specifically, which no retrieved study resolves with an isotope or selective-inhibition experiment.
 Batch112: the graph now uses exact-pair proteomic cultivation evidence rather than the 1998 M. hungatei passage as full support. Main-text Fdh1/Hox assignments are qualified mechanistic interpretations; no exact-pair hydrogen/formate flux ratio is inferred. The 2024 transcription passages were rechecked in the existing curator-supplied text; fresh publisher retrieval was unavailable. Hydrogen partial pressure is distinguished from formate concentration.

items.prompt: Which Brunner MSM salts, vitamins, and supplement concentrations were present in the sulfadiazine isotope-tracing coculture medium?

items.prompt: Keep energy sensing distinct from stimulus-defined taxis classes.
items.rationale: This entry follows the electron-transport-based usage in the cited primary studies. Energy generation powering motility alone is insufficient: changes must inform locomotor control. Aerotaxis, phototaxis and chemotaxis can involve other sensing mechanisms and are not automatically children or exact synonyms. Metabolism-dependent chemotaxis can instead sense intracellular intermediates, so that broader phrase is not an exact synonym. The existing flagellar-specific chemotaxis record is not used as a universal parent. Resolve external mappings at their authorities and compare process versus organismal-disposition scope before adding xrefs.

items.prompt: Which exact MDSC members acted as primary mucin glycan degraders, secondary degraders, and hydrogen consumers in each mucin condition?
items.rationale: The 2026 MDSC paper states that the community design included primary mucin degraders, secondary degraders, and hydrogen consumers and measured condition-level community composition, glycan degradation, and metabolite production. Pairwise member-to-member carbon or gas fluxes in the exact 14-strain MDSC were not resolved from this paper alone, so this record captures only community-level mucin responses.

items.prompt: Resolve RAZR natural hosts, phage ring triggers, RNA-substrate breadth, and model coverage before minting narrower RAZR mechanism children.
items.rationale: Zhang et al. support RAZR as a ring-activated zinc-finger HEPN RNase that can oligomerize around unrelated phage ring scaffolds, but natural locus breadth, the full phage-trigger set, exact RNA-substrate preference, and absence from the pinned DefenseFinder HMM/rules rows need further review.

Search-index membership and protocol leads are not verified source evidence. No deleted publication body is restored. Resolve each assay's member set, growth versus recovery conditions, moisture/salt attribution and pH mediation before strengthening the graph. The current repair qualifies existing descriptions only: three nodes, zero arrows and needs_research remain. Non-graph media, cultivation and aroma claims are preserved, not certified. items.prompt: Avoid asserting a microtubule-based mononeme transport mechanism until direct motor or route evidence is curated.
items.rationale: Singh et al. noted that the mononeme might move along microtubules and that testing this would require exact localization of the mononeme and candidate motors. The causal graph therefore records only observed topology and PfROM1 relocalization.

items.prompt: Resolve VP1796 native host breadth, exact single-component activity, profile-to-protein mapping, homolog boundary, full phage breadth, molecular output, and rule-level DefenseFinder criteria before minting narrower VP1796 mechanism children.
items.rationale: Getz et al. support VP1796 as one of nine RIMD 2210633 integron-encoded cassettes whose cloned expression reduced phage plaquing, Supplementary Tables 8, 9, and 12 map VP1796 to VP_RS08620/Vp1796, WP_005477844.1, VSV105-vp1796, and phage-plating fold changes, and Supplementary Data 1 reports PSI-BLAST homologs. The pinned DefenseFinder HMM inventory records one VP1796 custom profile row. The pinned rules table has no VP1796 row, and the first-pass record does not resolve native host breadth, complete phage breadth, direct profile-to-protein correspondence, molecular output, or endogenous activity.

items.prompt: Resolve exact source-neutral family groundings for cytostome-cytopharynx localized proteins before adding molecular components.
items.rationale: The first known T. cruzi cytostome-cytopharynx proteins were identified by localization rather than by a curated exact InterPro, Pfam, NCBIfam or UniProt family boundary in this pass.

items.prompt: Resolve exact source-neutral groundings for the Sm ring and U11-specific protein families that form the U11 snRNP.
items.rationale: The first GO:0005692 record captures U11 snRNA and the GO-defined Sm ring at coarse granularity. Individual spliceosomal Sm proteins and U11-specific protein-family boundaries should be resolved before splitting this inventory.

items.prompt: Add hypocone molecular components only after directly localized constituents and exact source-neutral family groundings have been identified.
items.rationale: GO defines the dinoflagellate hypocone as a subcellular region below the cingulum, but this pass did not find exact family-level evidence for hypocone-specific molecular constituents.

items.prompt: Resolve HEC-04 native host breadth, sensitive-phage breadth, ATPase-TOPRIM molecular output, and rule-level detection criteria before minting narrower HEC-04 mechanism children.
items.rationale: Payne et al. support HEC-04 as a single-gene Hma-embedded candidate anti-phage system whose ABC ATPase and nuclease domains are both required for defense, and the pinned DefenseFinder HMM inventory records one HEC-04 profile row. The pinned rules table has no HEC-04 row, and the first-pass record does not yet resolve natural host breadth, phage target breadth, or the direct molecular output.

items.prompt: Add antapex molecular components only after directly localized constituents and exact source-neutral family groundings have been identified.
items.rationale: GO defines the dinoflagellate antapex as a point of the hypocone, but this pass did not find exact family-level evidence for antapex-specific molecular constituents.

items.prompt: Keep neighboring cortical structures and proposed calcium-handling machinery outside the established constituent list.

items.prompt: Should FlgD, FlgK, or FlgL be curated as bacterial-type flagellum hook components?
items.rationale: The GO:0009424 hook record is scoped to the FlgE tube. FlgD forms the hook cap during assembly, and FlgK/FlgL form the hook-filament junction after hook completion; each is adjacent to, rather than part of, the mature hook.

items.prompt: Retain source discrepancies and resolve remaining construct mappings before transferring mechanisms.
items.rationale: HEPN superfamily membership does not establish this Pfam, and source numbering differs between experimental constructs and current references.

items.prompt: Resolve the exact medium formulation, inoculation ratio, temperature, atmosphere, and vessel used for the defined three-strain organic-nitrogen nitrifying community.
items.rationale: The cached PubMed abstract identifies the three NBRC strains, the organic-nitrogen function, nitrate/nitrite readouts, and RT-qPCR abundance tracking, but it does not report the exact organic nitrogen substrates, medium formulation, inoculation ratio, temperature, atmosphere, or vessel. Those cultivation details should be filled from the article Methods when an accessible full text is inspected.

items.prompt: How much of exudate pathogen suppression is caused by resource competition rather than antibiosis?
items.rationale: PMIDs:40223277 and 40468884 distinguish tissue disease scores from exudate pathogen counts. Biolog overlap and co-culture responses do not identify the active mechanism; predicted biosynthetic clusters are not chemically validated effectors. Preserve the separate strain-alias and effector gaps.

items.prompt: Extend array-associated machinery and isoform coverage only with direct membership and role evidence.
items.rationale: This is a bounded polymer inventory, not a complete HAA proteome. The Atb2 reference sequence is not the experimental strain. Beta-tubulin class composition does not justify an Nda3 example without an inspected isoform-specific experiment. Dynein-dynactin participates in movement, but its detailed array-resident composition and assembly essentiality need separate primary-source review before adding machinery rows. Unpublished observations about dynein-assisted radial rearrangement and suggested Hrs1/NudE similarity in the 2012 Discussion are not treated as verified family or component assignments.

items.prompt: Resolve exact component groundings for Plasmodium food vacuole proteases, proton pumps and solute transporters.
items.rationale: This first record models the digestive-vacuole membrane as an aggregate. Follow-up curation should split experimentally localized Plasmodium vacuolar hydrolases, PfCRT, Pgh1 and acidification machinery only where exact source-neutral families or species-specific UniProt examples can be verified.

items.prompt: This structure is reported by more than one MIBiG entry: BGC0001779, BGC0001920. Confirm they describe the same compound rather than an upstream cross-reference error.
Retain unresolved historical adaptation and chemotaxis identity without reviving deprecated identifiers.
items.rationale: Pinned and inspected current METPO graphs mark METPO:0000248 and METPO:000249 Microbial Adaptation, METPO:1000004 adaptation and METPO:1000062 chemotaxis deprecated. Inspected subjects have no replacement or consider annotations; OMO:0001000 reasons are provisional under open METPO issue 521. Original historical scopes remain unresolved. Neither biological invalidity nor exact equivalence follows from their labels or deprecation reasons. This qualified external-trace phenotype is accepted independently from primary evidence. Ignored and hidden current files, available tracked history, independent copies, pending changes and inspected ontology graphs revealed no exact active record within the documented scope. No historical exact mapping is asserted. Existing records and the pinned ontology remain unchanged; discovery is not exhausted.

items.prompt: Resolve Borvo phage triggers and effector outputs before minting narrower Borvo mechanism children.
items.rationale: Millman et al. and DefenseFinder support Borvo as a named anti-phage system with BovA profiles, but the trigger, molecular substrate, antiviral effector output, and subtype-specific mechanism are not resolved enough here to assert a narrower mechanistic child trait.

items.prompt: Extend the remaining Archease biochemical contexts with exact construct mappings.
items.rationale: The initial human and archaeal assays are not the whole family mechanism.

items.prompt: Resolve exact source-neutral groundings for nucleomorph chromosomes, the nucleomorph envelope, and any conserved nucleomorph pore or division machinery.
items.rationale: This first nucleomorph record curates the directly sequenced residual chromosomes as reviewed-label-only because generic chromosome terms are broader than nucleomorph chromosomes, and leaves lipid-envelope and protein-machinery composition unmodeled until exact cross-lineage constituent classes are verified.

items.prompt: What experimental evidence establishes the assigned proline configuration of the BGC0001422 HW-1 product?
items.rationale: The source-matching C44 graph yields R-proline in a virtual-hydrolysis calculation, while BGC0001422 predicts an S-proline substrate. Prediction does not establish final-product stereochemistry. The independent 2006 L-proline assignment concerns M. xanthus DK1050, not M. fulvus HW-1; the cited 2017 HW-1 full text was unavailable (HTTP403). Retain the assigned center, two undefined alanine centers, incomplete-stereo flag and imported evidence grades until exact-strain evidence is inspected. This qualification is not a stereo correction, experimental identity approval, or permission to merge the C45 owner.

items.prompt: Resolve Rst_HelicaseDUF2290 native host breadth, accession-level DUF2290/helicase roles, the DUF2290_Pers profile relationship, and the mechanism of T7 restriction before minting narrower Rst_HelicaseDUF2290 mechanism children.
items.rationale: Rousset et al. support a two-gene ATP-dependent helicase plus DUF2290 P4-hotspot system that inhibits T7 growth, and DefenseFinder represents Rst_HelicaseDUF2290 as a required two-profile model. This first system-level record leaves native host breadth, profile-to-gene mapping, the role of the extra DUF2290_Pers HMM profile, the molecular activities of the DUF2290 and helicase components, and the T7 restriction mechanism unresolved.

items.prompt: This structure is reported by more than one MIBiG entry: BGC0000939, BGC0001498, BGC0001499. Confirm they describe the same compound rather than an upstream cross-reference error.
Review route-inclusive scope and cargo-selective degradative flux.
items.rationale: Use autophagy traitmech:000638 as parent. The 2014 microautophagy study and the 2019 online/2020 issue ESCRT paper support a route-inclusive phenotype, whereas Mochida et al. 2015 use autophagy specifically for macroautophagy. GO:0061709 reticulophagy, resolved at https://www.ebi.ac.uk/QuickGO/services/ontology/go/terms/GO%3A0061709, is a nonobsolete biological process whose definition specifies autophagosomes and whose exact synonyms include ER-phagy. That route restriction and the process-to-phenotype shift prevent an exact xref here; retain the source-attributed difference for human review without silently narrowing the microbial phenotype. No synonyms or SSSOM mapping are asserted. ER stress, unfolded-protein responses, ER-associated protein degradation outside the lysosome/vacuole, bulk cytoplasmic turnover, gene presence, puncta or accumulated whorls alone are insufficient. Nuclear-envelope cargo can overlap nucleophagy without making the two traits equivalent.

items.prompt: Resolve construct and source discrepancies without treating broad-CTD assays as isolated Pfam mechanisms.
items.rationale: The experimental CTD is wider than the current Pfam match; extra-domain substitutions, affinity-label conflicts and tag differences limit attribution.

items.prompt: Resolve exact bacterial and eukaryotic acidocalcisome proton-pump and cation-transporter families rather than grouping all acidification and ion-transport proteins together.
items.rationale: The first record captures the transport roles required to maintain an acidic cation store, but V-H+-PPase, V-H+-ATPase and calcium transporter complements vary by lineage.

items.prompt: Refine the hierarchy while preserving the microbial actor and nematode movement endpoint.
items.rationale: This is the microorganism's attracting capability, not its own chemotaxis or a nematode's sensory trait. Passive retention, co-occurrence, trapping, paralysis, killing or consumption alone are insufficient; attraction need not imply any of those outcomes. Neither infection nor predatory intent is required. Phenotype METPO:1000059 is the conservative parent; the trap-formation, fungal-nematophagy and lethal-nematicidal records are related, not equivalents or necessary parents. Pinned/current METPO annotations and templates yielded no exact active or deprecated counterpart in the documented screen. v597 proposes the missing class. No exact synonyms, xrefs or organism-level disjointness are asserted.

items.prompt: Resolve PD-T7-4 natural host breadth, direct phage trigger, and PF13643-associated effector mechanism before minting narrower PD-T7-4 mechanism traits.
items.rationale: Vassallo et al. support PD-T7-4 as one of the conserved systems from an E. coli pangenome phage-defense selection, the DefenseFinder wiki maps the source locus to protection against SECphi18, SECphi27, T3, and T7, and DefenseFinder represents the system with one profile. Natural host breadth, the direct phage trigger, and effector logic remain unresolved.

ANA-3 (NCBITaxon:94122), but verified UniProtKB accessions and proteome metadata must be added to a GENE_OR_PROTEIN node before marking the graph MECHANISTIC.

items.prompt: Resolve exact component boundaries and source-neutral groundings for subpellicular microtubule end proteins, plus-end factors, and IMC particle-lattice linkers.

items.rationale: The first GO:0034693 record captures the GO-grounded U11 and U12 snRNP subparticles. Will, Schneider, Hossbach and colleagues identified multiple 18S U11/U12 proteins by mass spectrometry; their source-neutral family boundaries should be resolved before splitting that protein inventory.

items.prompt: Should MsbA be curated as a constituent of the lipopolysaccharide transport system?
items.rationale: MsbA flips nascent LPS across the inner membrane before the Lpt machine extracts LPS and transports it across the periplasm to the outer membrane. MsbA is therefore upstream of, rather than a constituent of, the Lpt transport system.

items.prompt: Review the proposed infection class without reviving the obsolete parasitism identifier.
items.rationale: No exact active counterpart was identified in inspected pinned/current releases, editor and six template owners. Historical METPO:1000227 obsolete parasitism is broader, deprecated, under ObsoleteClass with OMO:0001000 reason and no replacement or consider annotation in those releases. METPO issue 521 disputes mechanically assigned reasons; the code neither invalidates the biology nor authorizes reuse. The historical ID is not revived or placed in xrefs. The ontology pin remains unchanged; v603 proposes this narrower infection phenotype with PROPOSED status and no equivalent external xref. Existing bacterial endoparasitic predation is not this fungal spore-infection strategy.

items.prompt: Resolve exact source-neutral family groundings for the NuA3b constituents.
items.rationale: GO:1990468 defines five budding-yeast proteins as NuA3b constituents. Exact source-neutral InterPro, Pfam, NCBIfam or UniProt family boundaries for these NuA3b subunit classes need narrower curation before these component labels can be grounded.

items.prompt: Review other mapped YidD members without importing hemolysin or YidC annotations.
items.rationale: Selected E. coli experiments do not characterize the complete PF01809 family. The DUF31 caption conflicts with the study's DUF37 identity, and toxin-associated labels are not a functional assay of this family.
